series_note.statement: Batch 04 is the FIRST Kafka batch. It opens a domain the approved index has never touched: zero of the 85 applied concepts cite any Kafka source, and the index contains no messaging, streaming, broker, or event-log concept.
series_note.consequence: Unlike batches 02 and 03, batch 04 cannot be reasoned about as an extension of an existing namespace. Its concepts will occupy a new root namespace, and the collision surface against the applied index is thin by construction (see alias_scan_semantics).

predecessor_state.note: All three predecessor Book batches are applied and independently verified, so the approved index batch 04 must be authored against is fixed and knowable today.

contract.consumer: Executable batch manifest for `node tooling/brain/knowledge.mjs propose --batch`.
contract.consumer_status: EXECUTABLE. Carries a candidates[] array of 34 authored candidates and a rejected_candidates[] array of 3 scope-level rejection probes.
contract.engine_surface_verified: tooling/brain/knowledge.mjs sha256 f2af802a06750b4f9d3b6727e12e89629a0f5855b873a7e12b15bfd122ceaad6 exposes propose (--pilot | --batch), sample, verify, apply, promote and rollback. Batch mode requires >= 1 candidate and a batch_id matching /^[a-z0-9]+(?:[._-][a-z0-9]+)*$/, which `book-batch-04` satisfies.
contract.forbidden: This manifest must not be signed, applied, promoted or committed. It authorizes propose only; U3 generation, signature and apply are separate gates.

ordering.rule: repo-relative POSIX path, ascending byte-wise (LC_ALL=C) UTF-8 comparison
ordering.grouping: extraction sources first, then rejection probes; each group independently byte-sorted. Batch 04 has no file-level probes.

hash_lock.encoding: lowercase hex over complete raw-layer file bytes
hash_lock.batch_baseline_recipe: sha256 of the UTF-8 concatenation of `<role>\t<path>\t<source_sha256>\n` for every entry in order_index order
hash_lock.batch_baseline_reproduce: { for f in content/brain/books/kafka/chap01.md; do printf 'extraction\t%s\t%s\n' "$f" "$(shasum -a 256 "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)"; done; } | shasum -a 256
hash_lock.book_corpus_recipe: sha256 of the UTF-8 concatenation of `<path>\t<source_sha256>\n` for all 27 content/brain/books Markdown files in LC_ALL=C path order
hash_lock.batch_baseline_role: deterministic source baseline and sample-seed INPUT. It is NOT the AC-15 `sample.json` seed.
hash_lock.drift_policy: fail-closed. Re-verify every source_sha256 and approved_knowledge_tree_sha256_at_inventory immediately before propose and again before apply; a mismatch aborts. `apply` independently refuses with `approved knowledge content changed after proposal generation` if the knowledge tree moved.

line_count_definition: physical lines. A terminal newline terminates the last line and does not begin another; line_count is NOT `split("\n").length`.
evidence_class_definition: EXCLUSIVE classes: prose-bearing (prose_lines > 3), low-evidence-prose (0 < prose_lines <= 3), code-only (prose_lines = 0 AND code_lines > 0), zero-evidence (prose_lines = 0 AND code_lines = 0). Every scope has exactly one; the four counts partition the scope total.
positive_prose_definition: INCLUSIVE tally of scopes with prose_lines > 0 = prose-bearing + low-evidence-prose. It OVERLAPS the low-evidence class, is not an evidence_class, and is never part of the partition.

scope_class_accounting.rule: every scope belongs to exactly one evidence_class; the four exclusive class counts sum to the scope total
scope_class_accounting.positive_prose_is_not_a_class: positive_prose = 25 is the INCLUSIVE count of scopes with prose_lines > 0, i.e. prose-bearing (23) + low-evidence-prose (2). It is a forecasting base, not an evidence_class, and must never be added to the partition.

selection_budget.purpose: Batch 04 opens the Kafka series, whose chapters are individually far larger than any Do it! Java slice. A budget is stated BEFORE selection so the choice is falsifiable rather than a preference.

B1_bytes.basis: largest applied batch: book-batch-02 at 57,373 bytes

B2_heading_scopes.basis: largest applied batch: book-batch-02 at 65 scopes

B4_prose_lines.basis: largest applied batch: book-batch-02 at 329 prose lines, plus 10% headroom. Prose lines are the review-burden measure a U3 reviewer actually reads, and they are the budget that binds here.

why_not_more.statement: chap01 + chap02 satisfies B1, B2, B3 and B5 but reaches 181% of the prose-line ceiling — 651 prose lines against a 360 ceiling and against book-batch-02's realized 329. B4 binds, so chap02 is deferred. chap01 alone is therefore the MAXIMAL adjacency-preserving selection under the stated budget.

all_eight_do_not_fit.statement: The eight unmined Kafka substantive chapters total 331,664 bytes, 178 heading scopes and 2,940 prose lines — 8.2x the prose-line budget and 5.8x the largest applied batch by bytes. Every individual chapter consumes between 63% and 151% of the whole budget on its own. The Kafka series therefore needs roughly one batch per chapter, not one batch for the series.

alias_scan_semantics.purpose: Overlap is reported under BOTH scan identities with the identity stated, because they disagree and only one models the engine's collision behaviour.
alias_scan_semantics.key_naming_note: Alias lists here are keyed `applied_aliases` / `alias_identities`, never the reserved candidate key `aliases`. Every string recorded belongs to an ALREADY-APPLIED concept; none is authored.

literal_scan.identity: case-sensitive UTF-8 byte substring, no normalization
literal_scan.caveat: A byte metric only. It does NOT model the engine's collision identity.

collision_normalized_scan.identity: normalizedKey() from tooling/brain/knowledge-index.mjs: String(v).normalize('NFKC').trim().toLocaleLowerCase('en-US'), applied to both sides then substring-matched. This is the identity collisionReport() keys its title_or_alias bucket on.

alias_scan_semantics.verdict: All 7 touched applied concepts resolve to no_op. Four are substring or fenced-code artifacts (OS, OOP, Object, 필드-as-schema-field) and three are prose-anchored but domain-different (배열 as byte array, 인터페이스 as client/network interface, API as Kafka Connect API). Batch 04 opens an entirely new domain: ZERO of the 85 applied concepts cite any Kafka source, and the applied index contains no messaging, streaming, or broker concept.

rejection_probe_policy.justification: The Book corpus contains four frontmatter-only Markdown files: headfirst/chap01.md, kafka/chap03.md, kafka/chap04.md and the root landing page books/index.md. The three CHAPTER files were adopted as file-level rejection probes by book-batch-01, which APPLIED with all three recorded in rejected-candidates.json as insufficient-source-evidence with proposal_created false. Whole-document negative coverage is therefore already discharged against these exact, still-unchanged bytes, so batch 04 takes no file-level probe.

frontmatter_only_files.non_probe_reason: structural-landing-page; not a valid extraction or probe candidate under the evidence rule.

rejection_probe_policy.coverage_gap: none. File-level negative coverage is discharged by the applied book-batch-01 packet; scope-level negative coverage is supplied in-batch.

scope_level_rejection_probes.definition: heading scope whose body is non-substantive under the engine's substantiveBodyText() gate. For all batch-04 probes this coincides with prose_lines = 0 AND code_lines = 0; the engine gate is the authoritative criterion.

code_only_scopes.definition: heading scope with prose_lines = 0 AND code_lines > 0
code_only_scopes.note: Batch 04's selected source contains none, unlike batch 03. The code-only authoring hazard (P6 in batch 03) does not arise here.

selection_rationale.scheduling_hint: The book-batch-03 inventory scheduled batch 04+ as the Kafka substantive chapters (chap01, 02, 05, 07, 08, 09, 10, 14), split by byte budget. This lane executes the first slice of that plan and replaces 'byte budget' with the explicit five-ceiling budget in selection_budget, because bytes alone do not model review burden.
selection_rationale.primary: kafka/chap01.md (카프카 시작하기) is the series opener and the only chapter that defines the vocabulary every later chapter presupposes: message and batch, schema, topic and partition, producer and consumer, broker and cluster, retention and log compaction, multi-cluster. Starting anywhere else would forward-reference undefined terms, exactly the defect batches 02 and 03 were scoped to avoid.
selection_rationale.bounded: One extraction file, 25,915 bytes, 28 heading scopes of which 25 carry prose and 25 are engine-substantive, 321 prose lines. This is 43% of the byte ceiling and 89% of the prose-line ceiling — the binding constraint.
selection_rationale.adjacency: A single file trivially preserves per-file adjacency, and chap01 is the series opener with no predecessor to strand. chap02 remains directly adjacent and is the designated batch 05.
selection_rationale.probes: No file-level probes (discharged by the applied batch 01); 3 in-source zero-evidence scopes provide negative coverage.
rejected_alternatives: All eight Kafka chapters in one batch: 331,664 bytes / 178 scopes / 2,940 prose lines = 8.2x the prose-line ceiling and 5.8x the largest applied batch. Rejected on every ceiling.
chap01 + chap02 (the adjacent pair): satisfies B1, B2, B3 and B5 but reaches 181% of B4 at 651 prose lines. Rejected on the binding ceiling; chap02 becomes batch 05.
chap09 first (the smallest chapter, 228 prose lines): would fit comfortably but forward-references the entire chap01 vocabulary. Rejected on adjacency and dependency order.
A sub-chapter split of chap01: possible but unnecessary — chap01 fits the budget whole, and splitting a single chapter would strand its internal cross-references.

expected_candidate_profile.disclaimer: Ranges and topics only. No concept_id, title, canonical_path, alias, or tag is authored here for any new concept.
expected_candidate_profile.forecast_base: positive_prose (INCLUSIVE, prose_lines > 0) = 25. This is the base batch 01 (31), batch 02 (53) and batch 03 (30) were measured on, so the ratios below are comparable.
expected_candidate_profile.range_derivation: Realized ratios per positive-prose scope: batch 01 17/31 = 0.548, batch 02 34/53 = 0.642, batch 03 28/30 = 0.933. The band 0.548-0.933 applied to 25 positive-prose scopes gives 13.7-23.3, i.e. 14-23. CONFIDENCE IS LOW AND THE RANGE IS A FLOOR, for a reason batches 01-03 did not have: batch-04 scopes are far denser (12.8 prose lines per positive-prose scope versus 9.4 / 6.2 / 4.6), and five scopes carry 20 or more prose lines each. A dense scope typically supports more than one concept, so the true centre is likely at or above the top of this band. The per-prose-line basis is recorded and explicitly NOT used: its realized ratios (0.058 / 0.103 / 0.203) vary by 3.5x and would forecast 19-65, which is too wide to be actionable.
expected_candidate_profile.ratio_instability_note: The per-positive-prose-scope ratio has risen monotonically across batches (0.548 -> 0.642 -> 0.933) because slice granularity has been getting finer, not because the method improved. Treat 14-23 as a planning floor and gate the authoring lane on the candidate ceiling B5 = 38 rather than on this range.

existing_touch_points.collision_handling_rule: Every touch point below is no_op: batch 04 must NOT update, merge into, or re-mint any of them. Where a Kafka-domain concept covers the same WORD (배열 as byte array, 인터페이스 as client interface, API as Kafka Connect API), it must carry a distinct title and alias set and relate rather than restate. collisionReport() keys title_or_alias under NFKC+lowercase, so re-using 배열 / 인터페이스 / API / 객체 as a bare title would collide and fail the proposal build.

existing_touch_points.verified_absent_overlap: ZERO of the 85 applied concepts cite any Kafka source. expected_flagged_for_full_review.rule: plan §5.1 requires 100% review of conflict / low-confidence / provenance-warning proposals; REVIEW_FLAGS in knowledge.mjs is exactly {conflict, low-confidence, provenance-warning}.
expected_flagged_for_full_review.dense_scope_expectation: The 5 scopes carrying 20 or more prose lines should be expected to yield multiple candidates each, and any candidate whose locator covers only part of such a scope should be checked for an unsupported granularity claim — the defect that produced R1/R2 in the batch-03 candidate review.
expected_flagged_for_full_review.sample_quota_recipe: computeBatchSample() sets quota = min(unflagged_pool, max(5, ceil(0.10 x unflagged_pool))) over the UNFLAGGED pool; category coverage can add one draw per proposal kind missing from the quota slice, so the discretionary count is a floor.
expected_flagged_for_full_review.estimated_u3_review_load: ESTIMATE ONLY. Batch 03 realized 20 mandatory of 28 after its repair; batch 02 sampled 18 of 34. With only 2 low-evidence scopes and no code-only scopes, batch 04's flagged set will be driven by conflict and provenance-warning decisions made during authoring rather than by scope class, so no numeric estimate is asserted here.

preconditions.statement: All three predecessor Book batches are applied and independently verified, so candidate authoring is not sequencing-blocked.
preconditions.resolution: Bind approved_knowledge_tree_sha256_at_inventory into the future batch manifest and re-verify before propose and before apply.

preconditions.statement: The approved knowledge tree must not move between this inventory and batch-04 apply. It is fcd973c16ed07ce109f7676de9d72bcd77dd5bd6aacea2f40a4d843012bf36ea (86 files, 85 concepts).
preconditions.consequence: Any intervening apply forces regeneration; `apply` refuses with `approved knowledge content changed after proposal generation`. Fail-closed, not a corruption risk.
preconditions.resolution: Sequence batch 04 as the only in-flight Book packet, or regenerate after any intervening apply.

preconditions.statement: The raw layer is uncommitted; the extraction source is untracked in git, so drift cannot be caught by git alone.
preconditions.resolution: Re-verify all 27 corpus source_sha256 immediately before propose and again before apply; fail closed on mismatch.

preconditions.statement: Tag policy: knowledge tags[] must equal canonical_path folder segments; `brain` and `knowledge` are reserved. Raw Kafka frontmatter carries the display tag `📚 카프카 핵심가이드`.
preconditions.resolution: Derive tags from canonical_path folders only; never copy the display tag.

preconditions.statement: Alias policy H-1: knowledge aliases are search-only; `aliases`/`alias`/`permalink` are forbidden in knowledge frontmatter.
preconditions.resolution: Use knowledge_aliases plus the KNOWLEDGE_ALIASES body block, as all 85 applied concepts do.

preconditions.statement: Batch 04 opens a new root namespace and the authoring lane must choose it. This inventory deliberately does not.
preconditions.consequence: An inconsistent or late namespace choice would force re-authoring of every candidate, since concept_id and canonical_path are both derived from it.
preconditions.resolution: Fix the Kafka root namespace as the first authoring decision, record it in the candidate manifest's rationale, and check every proposed title and alias against the 7 occupied normalized keys listed above.

preconditions.statement: Scope density is unprecedented: 12.8 prose lines per positive-prose scope, with 5 scopes at 20 or more prose lines (largest 39).
preconditions.consequence: The 14-23 candidate forecast is a floor, and a candidate citing only part of a dense scope can easily claim more than its span supports — the exact defect flagged as R1/R2 in the batch-03 candidate review.
preconditions.resolution: Expect multiple candidates per dense scope, and check every granularity clause against its own cited span before U3.

namespace_decision.rule: kafka.* for Kafka-specific concepts; messaging.* only for genuinely technology-agnostic messaging concepts with direct evidence.
namespace_decision.deferred_extraction: Serialization formats (Avro/Protobuf/JSON) are filed under kafka.schema.* because this chapter introduces them as Kafka's schema options. Rule 4 of the namespace decision permits extracting them to a technology-agnostic root during consolidation; extraction adds concepts and never moves them.
namespace_decision.folder_route_rule: collisionReport() rejects a document whose filename stem equals its parent folder name. Seven leaves were renamed accordingly (kafka-broker, kafka-message, kafka-origin, message-retention, kafka-schema, kafka-stream, kafka-topic), following the applied precedent java.array.array -> java/array/java-array.md and software.api.api -> software/api/application-programming-interface.md. concept_id is unchanged; the engine imposes no id-path mirroring rule.

occupied_key_policy.rule: No candidate title or alias may normalize to a key already held by an applied concept. All seven touch points remain no_op; this batch authors no update and no merge against any applied concept.

scope_accounting.rule: Every heading scope is either proposed (at least one accepted candidate locator lies inside it) or rejected (a scope-level rejection probe cites it). No scope is unaccounted.

candidates.title: 메세지

candidates.title: 메세지 키

candidates.title: 배치
candidates.concept_granularity: single grouping of messages written to one topic partition together to trade latency for throughput

candidates.title: 스키마

candidates.title: 직렬화 포맷

candidates.title: 토픽
candidates.concept_granularity: single Kafka classification of messages, composed of partitions and comparable to a database table

candidates.title: 파티션
candidates.concept_granularity: single append-only log within a topic that guarantees order inside itself and provides redundancy and horizontal scale

candidates.title: 스트림
candidates.concept_granularity: single continuous flow of the data held in one topic, moving from producer to consumer in contrast with offline batch frameworks

candidates.title: 카프카 클라이언트

candidates.title: 프로듀서

candidates.title: 컨슈머
candidates.concept_granularity: single Kafka client that subscribes to topics and reads partition messages in written order, tracking how far it has read

candidates.title: 오프셋
candidates.concept_granularity: single integer position metadata Kafka assigns to each message so a consumer can record progress and resume after its last read message

candidates.title: 컨슈머 그룹
candidates.concept_granularity: single group of cooperating consumers in which each partition is read by exactly one member, giving horizontal scale and failover

candidates.title: 브로커
candidates.concept_granularity: single Kafka server that assigns offsets, writes messages to disk and serves partition read requests

candidates.title: 클러스터
candidates.concept_granularity: single group of brokers, one of which is elected controller, that scales without losing availability

candidates.title: 파티션 리더
candidates.concept_granularity: single partition-leader role: the broker responsible for a partition, replaced by a follower after leader failure within the same cluster

candidates.title: 메세지 보존
candidates.concept_granularity: single durability rule holding messages for a configured time or partition size before expiry

candidates.title: 로그 압착
candidates.concept_granularity: single retention mode keeping only the most recent message per key, suited to change-log data

candidates.title: 다중 클러스터
candidates.concept_granularity: single multi-cluster deployment model separating data by type, isolation, or disaster recovery, including active-active mirroring across independent clusters

candidates.title: 미러메이커
candidates.concept_granularity: single cross-cluster mirroring tool that is itself only a Kafka consumer and producer joined by a queue

candidates.title: 다중 프로듀서
candidates.concept_granularity: single platform property accepting multiple producers across one or more topics while allowing a shared format and a unified consumer stream where the application chooses one common topic

candidates.title: 다중 컨슈머
candidates.concept_granularity: single platform property letting many consumers read the same stream without interference, unlike a single-delivery queue

candidates.title: 디스크 기반 보존
candidates.concept_granularity: single platform property storing messages durably on disk so consumers need not read in real time

candidates.concept_granularity: single platform property of growing from one small cluster to many brokers without losing availability

candidates.title: 고성능

candidates.title: 내고장성
candidates.concept_granularity: single platform property of continuing correct operation while individual components fail

candidates.title: 플랫폼 기능
candidates.concept_granularity: single pair of built-in platform features — Connect for system integration and Streams for stream processing

candidates.title: 데이터 생태계
